title: Game correction page
description: One game, across every store it appears on. Applied to the parsed TOML of games/<slug>.toml; the file name is a human label, and the page's key is the canonical id in its gamedb field.

title.description: The game's own capitalization, as the store or the game itself writes it.

year.description: Release year. The standard way to tell two games apart that share a title, and the qualifier a file name uses when it has to carry one.

gamedb.description: This page's canonical id. Derived where an authority already names the game: steam-<appid>, then the umu id, then a store codename (gog-1660194629, egs-Calluna) taking stores in the order gog, egs, ubisoft, ea, battlenet, amazon, humble, itchio, zoomplatform. Minted as gamedb-<uid> only when nothing names it, and a minted id must contain a letter so it cannot be mistaken for an authority's number. The prefix names the namespace the identifier belongs to; a consumer reads the prefix, never the shape of what follows. Assigned once, from the precedence above, and then frozen: a page that later learns a better identifier records it in [ids] and keeps the id it already had.

merged_from.description: Ids this page absorbed, when two pages turned out to be one game. They stay reserved forever: never reused for a different game, and carried into the built artifacts as aliases so an old lookup still resolves.

variant_of.description: The base game's canonical id, when this page is a separately sold product with its own store identity (a remaster, a definitive edition). Editions that are only another SKU of the same game are store entries on ONE page, not a page of their own.

ids.description: Identifiers in other people's namespaces, recorded as facts. None of them is this page's key: the canonical id is the gamedb field, taken from the precedence described there and frozen once assigned.

umu.description: Present only when the game IS in umu-database. A game umu declined has no umu id, and inventing one here would claim membership it does not have.

exe.description: Executable basenames that identify this game, for a page that has no store identity at all - a correction to somebody else's wrong row, say. This is the only case where nothing can be derived, and therefore the only case where a gamedb id is minted.

stores.description: Keyed by umu's own store spelling. Omitted only by a page identified purely by executable.

codename.description: The launcher-facing product identifier: an Epic app name, a GOG product id, a Steam app id.

exe.description: Basename or path as observed. Recorded only where it was actually seen for THIS store's copy.

edition.description: Which edition this store product is, when a store sells more than one and they are the same game (Standard, Deluxe, Game of the Year).
